stem.en: An elephant is much larger than a mouse. What is the main reason for this difference in size?

text.en: Each elephant cell is thousands of times bigger than a mouse cell.

feedback.en: Cells can grow only up to a certain size, in both animals.

text.en: An elephant has a far greater number of cells.

feedback.en: Yes. A bigger body has more cells, not much bigger ones.

text.en: Elephant cells have thick, heavy walls that add to its mass.

feedback.en: Animal cells have no cell wall.

text.en: Mouse cells keep shrinking, while elephant cells keep their size.

feedback.en: Mouse cells do not keep shrinking as the mouse grows.

explanation.en: Cells can grow only up to a certain size. A large animal is large because cell division has given it far more cells.

hints.en: Does a body grow mainly by making its cells bigger or by making more of them?
